title: Terraform module: secure egress + private DNS federation with upgrade & health probes
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement a reusable Terraform module that codifies secure egress policies (security groups + NACL patterns), private DNS zone federation for service discovery, and in-band health probe hooks to enable safe rolling upgrades in Private (VPC) deployments. The module will be consumed by Redwood Private stacks and by Dedicated clusters deployed in customer VPCs. Goal is to provide a single, well-documented IaC primitive that enforces least-privilege egress, prevents accidental internet exposure of internal services, supports private DNS cross-account federation, and exposes upgrade-safe health check endpoints. This ticket covers design, implementation, test harness, documentation, and initial rollout to staging stacks.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module written using canonical module layout and published to internal registry (module path: redwood/private-vpc/secure-egress-dns)
Security groups and NACLs are parameterized and default to deny-all-everywhere with explicit allow lists for known egress IPs, ports, and Redwood-managed services
PrivateRoute53 zones can be registered and federated across accounts via shared zone delegation or Resolver endpoints depending on cloud provider, controlled via module inputs
Module exposes outputs for required gateways (egress_proxy_endpoint, resolver_rule_id, health_probe_endpoint) and IAM role ARNs as strings
Automated health probe Lambda (or comparable probe) is deployed when enabled and reports pass/fail to a dashboard and RFC 3339 timestamp output

Module includes an upgrade-hook mechanism: a configurable tag/lock resource and pre-flight checks that prevent Terraform apply from cutting over DNS delegations or removing egress rules until health probes pass for X minutes
Integration test in staging validates that deploying a new runtime version with module enabled preserves existing connections and fails fast if health checks degrade
Comprehensive README, examples (single-account, cross-account/federation), and migration notes for existing stacks that use earlier egress modules
technical_notes: Trade-offs considered: use of AWS Route53 Resolver rules vs. shared hosted zone delegation; we will support both via input flag to accommodate on-premise-like customer topologies
NACLs are included for defense-in-depth in public subnets, but defaults favor security groups for simplicity; provide explicit examples to avoid double-allow pitfalls

Egress policy model: preferred pattern is egress-proxy endpoint + allowlist of internal CIDRs and service FQDNs resolved to IP prefixes at deploy-time; fallback to explicit IP ranges when customers disallow outbound DNS resolution

Health probe implementation: small Lambda / Fargate task that attempts TCP/HTTP checks and writes status to a DynamoDB /cloudwatch metric; using a managed probe reduces drift across regions and avoids depending on application health endpoints during upgrades

Upgrade hooks: implement pre_apply validation using terraform external data source to call the health-check endpoint and fail early if degraded; additionally, a short-lived lock resource (s3 dynamodb lock tag) will gate DNS changes
Backward compatibility: include migration helper script to translate allowlist format from existing modules (csv -> list) and a TF import guide for prior security group IDs
Observability: emit CloudWatch metrics and an event to our internal status dashboard (link in links) so on-call can see probe history during rollouts
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): module implemented and unit-tested in dev account; code review and security review checklist completed
Phase 2 (staging): deploy to staging Private stacks and run 48h soak with intentional fault injection (simulate egress endpoint failure) to verify rollback behavior
Phase 3 (canary): enable module in 2 customer-like Dedicated regions with traffic redirected through egress proxy; monitor latency/cost impact for 1 week
Phase 4 (general): publish module to internal registry, update templates, announce migration path in internal docs and runbooks
discussion_comments: 2026-02-12 - Marcus Patel: Initial spike complete. Prototype uses Route53 Resolver outbound endpoints + resolver rules for cross-account. Found complication when customer uses overlapping CIDRs; adding support for resolver endpoints in place of delegation as an option.

2026-02-16 - Security Review (Priya Rao): Request to ensure all IAM actions are scoped to resource ARNs and to document blast radius; also asked for threat model for health probe component. Marked security_review_required=true.

2026-02-20 - Ava Chen: Decided to implement the health probe as an optional construct (enabled by default) that can be switched to an external monitoring integration. Probe writes to CloudWatch metric 'private_egress_probe_status'.

2026-02-25 - Marcus Patel: Implemented pre-flight check via terraform external provider that queries the probe endpoint. This is a soft gate; we will make it a hard fail only after 2 canaries succeed.

2026-03-02 - Design Feedback (Lina Gomez): UX request to expose simple boolean 'allow_internet' plus fine-grained allowlist. Also requested example for customers needing HTTP proxy vs socket-level egress proxy.

2026-03-05 - QA (Diego Martins): Added integration tests to simulate egress proxy outage and verify that rolling upgrade is canceled and previous security group rules are preserved. Tests found an edge case with NACL rule numbering; fixed rule ordering in module.
2026-03-09 - Marcus Patel: PR #428 opened for initial implementation. Requesting a review from infra-security and platform-templates teams. Next steps: finalize README and run staging soak.
2026-03-10 - Ava Chen: Updated acceptance criteria to require outputs for health_probe_endpoint and resolver_rule_id. Marking this ticket In Progress and targeting staging rollout by 2026-03-24.
